question.worked_solution:
To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The logarithm is a natural logarithm, which means its base is $e.$ So, we use a base of $e$ for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{x}{3}) & =3 \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x/3)} & ={e}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x/3)}=\frac{x}{3}.$ 

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{3} & ={e}^{3} \\ x & =3{e}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$
